title: Repeated inner-scan work as loop count grows
method: Synthetic inner scan averages 0.2 ms per loop. Multiplying by 100,1,000 and 10,000 gives 20,200 and 2,000 ms of repeated work. Parent-inclusive timing, other operations and parallel overlap prevent treating these values as universal wall-clock totals.
alt: Repeated inner-scan work as loop count grows. 100 loops: 20 milliseconds; 1,000 loops: 200 milliseconds; 10,000 loops: 2000 milliseconds. Illustrative values.
